description: Returns OHLCV bars from `1s` to monthly for one ticker or a comma list of up to 50 in the path, such as a screen's matches.

adjusted.description: Default `true`: prices are split-adjusted (restated after each later split, as the tape is), so a series is continuous across a split. `false` returns the price as it printed that day (a name that later did a 1:10 reverse split reads `21.4` adjusted and `2.14` on the tape), which is what a broker fill or a chart from that time shows. Volume scales the other way.

asof.description: Point-in-time: the most recent bar whose period had closed at or before that moment. A bare `YYYY-MM-DD` means that day's close. A full timestamp means the last finished bar: at 10:00 ET on a Wednesday the day's close has not happened, so `1d` returns Tuesday's bar. A bare date on an intraday grid (`1m`, `1h`, …) is accepted and means the last bar of that day: the ET calendar day for stocks and ETFs (through the 19:59 ET bar), the UTC day for crypto, FX and rates. Returns one bar unless you also pass `limit`, which gives the last `limit` closed bars; follow `next_cursor` with the same parameters to keep paging back: the cursor and `asof` both bound the page, so no bar after the instant is ever served and every page stays on the company that held the symbol at the instant. Unlimited depth. Response time: under 1.5 s cold, under 0.6 s warm.

cursor.description: Continue paging back: the previous response's `next_cursor`, unchanged, with the same parameters. On a comma list, `next_cursor` is an object of each symbol's oldest-bar time; to page one symbol further, send its value as `cursor` with that symbol alone. From 2027-01-12 a comma list's `next_cursor` is one opaque string to pass back as `cursor` with the same symbols (Deprecations). A blank `cursor=` counts as absent.

from.description: Window start: `YYYY-MM-DD`, ISO timestamp or epoch milliseconds (11 to 13 digits). A bare date starts at the beginning of that day; a timestamp is included. Combines with `to` for an explicit window; page within it using `cursor`. Mutually exclusive with `asof` (400). See Time windows.

interval.description: Bar interval. `2h`/`4h` roll up hourly bars; `1w`/`1mo` roll up daily bars into calendar weeks (Monday start) and months; the bar's `t` is the bucket start (UTC), and with `asof` the last bucket is the week/month to date.

limit.description: Most-recent N bars. Max 1000; an over-cap value is clamped, not an error. On a comma list the cap is per symbol: each symbol returns its newest `limit` bars in the window.

session.description: Sub-hour intervals only. `all` (default) includes pre- and post-market bars. `regular` keeps bars whose start is in 09:30–16:00 ET (DST-aware). Why you might want it: the vendor buckets trades by SIP report time, and late-reported off-exchange (Form T) prints on thin names can land 20 min to hours late in a pre-market minute (a `$1.70` print at 08:13 ET on a `$3.85` stock). Daily high/low are untouched by those. `limit` counts after the filter; paging still works.

ticker.description: One symbol, or a comma-separated list of up to 50 for a response keyed by symbol. Case-insensitive. Equities are bare symbols (`NVDA`); every other class carries a prefix: rates (`R:SOFR`), crypto (`X:BTCUSD`), fx (`X:EURUSD`). Bare `BTC`/`ETH` are US-listed ETFs, not spot crypto. See Tickers.

to.description: Window end: `YYYY-MM-DD`, ISO timestamp or epoch milliseconds (11 to 13 digits). A bare date covers that whole day. A timestamp is included until 2027-01-12 (the newest bar returned is at or before it) and exclusive from then, as everywhere else (Deprecations). On sub-daily intervals a bare date on `from` or `to` is the ET calendar day for stocks and ETFs (the whole 04:00-20:00 ET session) and the UTC day for crypto, FX and rates. Mutually exclusive with `asof` (400). See Time windows.

name: tickerbot_get_bars
